turbosort/523f907:
The 17 to 512 tier ran a quicksort with 16-element leaves and lost to
std::sort_unstable across the whole range (0.69x at 128, 0.67x at 512).
Build bitonic networks over 4, 8, and 16 AVX2 registers on top of the
existing sort_network_8 and merge primitives, route 17 to 128 straight
to padded networks, and grow the quicksort leaf from 16 to 128 so the
recursion bottoms out in the network rather than insertion sort.

Measured on an i7-8665U against std in the same run: 128 elements go
from 0.69x to 2.3x, 512 from 0.67x to 1.4x. Randomized 0-1-principle and
distinct-value tests cover every length and network tier.

noodles/525dde6:
The KEY button opens a wheel instead of two dropdowns. Majors ride
the outer ring, relative minors the inner, and the current key's
seven diatonic chords light up as a contiguous function-colored
sector - IV/I/V over ii/vi/iii with vii-dim as a thin sliver on the
dominant edge, since its root has no honest station of its own. The
wheel never rotates; changing key drags the sector around fixed
stations by the rim, with the accidentals lighting in arrival order
during the drag and a canceled drag committing nothing. Taps sound
at the immediate clock (the tapTime lesson), holds bloom diatonic
extensions with names in the center hole, drags strum, and the
sheet's arm dot lets a clean tap replace the chord being heard in
the playing clip - bar-quantized by construction. Playback chords
draw a fading trail whose weight is the shared-tone count between
moves, so near-on-the-circle-means-smooth is visible instead of
taught. Rendering is a cached static layer composited under rAF
that only runs while the sheet is open and something moves; the
smoke gate gains a section driving the armed punch, the rim travel,
the trail, and the undo of the whole excursion.
site/52936d5:
No repo list to maintain: any project in projects.js with a github URL
is synced, and one whose README lacks a status line or a weak-spots
section keeps its hand-written entry. So adding a project is a normal
entry, and improving a README is what makes the card follow.

npm run add:project -- <repo> scaffolds an entry with the content
fields already pulled from that repo's README and tells you what the
README still needs. npm run readmes:report shows conformance across the
whole site.

All ten projects now sync. The weak-spots section accepts documented
aliases, because mentl's 'What is honestly unfinished' is better
writing than a forced rename, and the invariant is that the losses are
stated, not the heading.
